subject.title: RFC: Per-session tool policies — bridging operator scopes and agent tool access

question: Should gateway operator scopes become an input to agent tool-policy resolution, and if so where should the new scope-aware policy contract live?
rationale: The request would define a new authorization boundary across Gateway auth, agent tool filtering, config precedence, and multi-user trust semantics; automation cannot safely choose those security guarantees or config defaults.

options.title: Design scope-aware tool policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers approve a typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent contract, enforcement layer, precedence rules, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Use existing session/sender primitives
options.body: Route the need through `toolsBySender`, session envelopes, requester-origin hooks, or conversation identity modes instead of adding operator-scope-based config.

options.title: Decline scope-based RBAC
options.body: Document operator scopes as control-plane only and direct multi-user isolation to separate Gateways or a broader tenant RBAC design.

recommendation.title: Design scope-aware tool policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers approve a typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent contract, enforcement layer, precedence rules, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across scoped conversation profiles, operator-scope documentation, and sender-policy hardening adjacent to this boundary.
